title: One settled-status predicate, and the MCP sprint tools work again
description: Five production readers each hardcode one of the two terminal words, and the ones that picked "passed" return empty against a corpus of 250 contracts holding zero of them. Ship one predicate, migrate every reader to it, and pin the live bug closed. No writer changes here, so no conformance field moves — this sprint is pure reader convergence and it is immediately valuable on its own.

successCriteria.description: A single exported predicate decides whether a contract status is terminal. It generalises what updateContractStatus (src/contracts/sprint-contract.ts:216-219) and resume-cursor.ts:22 already do independently, rather than adding a third rule.

Every production reader doing a terminal check uses the predicate: src/mcp/tools/sprint.ts:147, src/mcp/tools/eval.ts:139, src/cli/commands/sprint.ts:160, src/cli/commands/eval.ts:127, src/state/history.ts:193. Readers that are NOT terminal checks (playwright.ts:530's test status, fleet/do-bridge run states, mcp/tools/status.ts:69's RunState) must be left alone — verify each before touching it.
A test drives both MCP sprint tools against the committed contract corpus and asserts a NON-EMPTY settled list. This is the live bug; it must be pinned, not merely fixed.

A test asserts no production module outside the predicate compares a contract status to a status literal for a terminal check, so a sixth reader cannot reintroduce the bug. Proven to bite by mutation.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green, and the golden gate still passes 6/6.

nonGoals: Changing what any writer writes — that is sprints 3 and 5.
stopConditions: A reader turns out not to be a terminal check after all — leave it and say so, rather than forcing it through the predicate.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: Do NOT blanket-replace every status comparison. The map is deliberate: mcp/tools/status.ts:69, fleet/reporter.ts, fleet/aggregator.ts and do-bridge/reconcile.ts compare RUN states, not contract statuses, and playwright.ts:530 compares a TEST result. Only the five named readers are contract-terminal checks. resume-cursor.ts:22 already reads both words — it is the shape to generalise, and it should end up calling the predicate too. Put the predicate next to ContractStatusSchema in src/contracts/sprint-contract.ts so it ships with the type it describes.
evaluatorNotes: The failure mode is over-reach: a blanket replace that catches run states or test results. Check each of the four non-contract sites listed in generatorNotes is untouched. Then verify sc-1-3 against the REAL corpus, not a fixture — count the settled contracts yourself and confirm the tools return that many. Verify sc-1-4 bites by adding a literal comparison in a temp copy.
